title: Split reductive points lift across quotients of a local ring
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal. An $A$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] with base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A reductive $A$-group scheme here means a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme with reductive geometric fibres: over every algebraically closed field a fibre is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Write $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. For an $A$-algebra $B$, $H(B)$ means $A$-scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\to H$, with the induced group law. A cocharacter is an $A$-group homomorphism $\mathbf G_{m,A}\to H$. Let $H$ be a reductive $A$-group scheme and $S\hookrightarrow H$ a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] with a specified isomorphism $S\simeq\mathbf G_{m,A}^{r}$, $r\geq0$, whose geometric fibres are maximal tori. A torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$, maximal for subgroup inclusion. Then the homomorphism $H(A)\to H(A/J)$ induced by the quotient map $A\to A/J$ is surjective. No henselianity or completeness of $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-reductive-local-gauss-atlas] to $(A,H,S)$ with exactly the hypotheses in the statement. Obtain open charts $\theta_i:V\to H$ covering $H$, where $V=\operatorname{Spec}A[x_1,\ldots,x_d,z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$. This is relative structure over $A$, rather than structure over an algebraic closure of its residue field.

proof.text: Put $B=A/J$ and let $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to H$ be an $A$-point. Every maximal ideal of $B$ pulls back to a maximal ideal of $A$, so $B$ is nonzero local with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/J$. Choose a chart image $U_i$ containing the image of this closed point under $h$. The open $h^{-1}(U_i)$ contains the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, hence is the whole spectrum: it contains a basic open $D(b)$ containing that point; then $b\notin\mathfrak m/J$, so $b$ is a unit and $D(b)=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $U_i$ is the open subscheme isomorphic to $V$. Restricting the structure-sheaf map of $h$ to this open gives a morphism $\widetilde h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ with $\theta_i\widetilde h=h$. This is the explicit open-factorization argument in the proof of Stacks 01J6, not a lifting assertion from smoothness.

source.place: Tag 01J6, lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring, last paragraph of proof; elementary application to the chart atlas, followed by explicit quotient-coordinate lifting.

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\widetilde h$ corresponds to an $A$-algebra map from the displayed Laurent-polynomial algebra to $B$. Write $\bar a_j\in B$ for the images of $x_j$ and $\bar u_l\in B^\times$ for the images of $z_l$. Choose lifts $a_j,u_l\in A$, and lift $\bar u_l^{-1}$ to $v_l\in A$. Then $u_lv_l=1+j_l$ for some $j_l\in J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The element $1+j_l$ is outside $\mathfrak m$ (otherwise subtract $j_l$), hence is a unit in the local ring $A$. Thus $u_l$ is a unit with inverse $v_l(1+j_l)^{-1}$. Sending $x_j\mapsto a_j$, $z_l\mapsto u_l$ and $z_l^{-1}\mapsto u_l^{-1}$ defines an $A$-algebra map to $A$: all relations $z_lz_l^{-1}=1$ hold. Its composite with $A\to B$ is exactly the map of $\widetilde h$, on constants and on every generator.

source.place: Tag 01J6, lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring, last paragraph of proof; elementary application to the chart atlas, followed by explicit quotient-coordinate lifting.

proof.text: Contravariant functoriality of the affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] turns this algebra map into an $A$-point $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to V$ reducing exactly to $\widetilde h$. Therefore $g=\theta_i v\in H(A)$ reduces to $\theta_i\widetilde h=h$. Since $h$ was arbitrary, the reduction homomorphism is surjective. With no polynomial or torus coordinates the same construction uses the unique map on the empty list; $J=0$, $J=\mathfrak m$, and $H=1$ are included.

The item statement is byte-identical to the base copy in the Q143 snapshot; only the proof fields and split_report changed. The atlas statement is true: Spec A is local, hence connected, and S is split, so the roots are constant and the root lines are free. So (H,S) is split in the sense of Conrad Def 5.1.1. Conrad Cor 5.1.11 gives Weyl representatives in N(S)(A). Conrad Thm 5.1.13 gives the open cell U^- x S x U^+, isomorphic to affine space times G_m^r. Its translates by the Weyl representatives cover every geometric fibre, because they are preimages of the opposite big cells of G/B at the points wB. I tested H=1, H=G_m^r, SL2 (the a-invertible and c-invertible charts) and GLn. The atlas statement contains no J, quotient or lifting, so it is not a restatement of the item. Item steps: step 1 applies the atlas with matching hypotheses. Step 2 works because an open set containing the closed point of local Spec A/J is the whole spectrum, so the point factors through the open subscheme given by def-weil-open-immersion. Step 3 lifts coordinates; units lift because uv=1+j with j in m, which is a unit. Step 4 gives the lift by Spec functoriality. Edge cases J=0, J=m, Z_(p) with J=(p), k[eps] and empty variable lists all go through. No henselian or nilpotence hypothesis is used.
